text:
Carter Mazur waited a long time for his first NHL goal, and Detroit made it count. Drafted 70th overall in 2021, he put the Red Wings ahead 1-0 in the first period on a wrist shot our numbers gave only a 3 percent chance of going in. Detroit went on to a 5-3 win in Florida that ended the Panthers' three-game winning streak.

By how the game was played, it should not have ended that way. Florida controlled the first period, out-chancing Detroit 2.16 to 0.49 in expected goals (a measure of shot quality), and finished with 69 shot attempts to 46. Over the full game, our simulations of every shot gave the Panthers a 68 percent chance to win, and Detroit's 32 percent was the smaller share. Detroit's counterpunch came in the second period, when it held the edge 1.72 to 0.83 in expected goals, and its goaltender helped. Daniil Tarasov stopped 23 of 26 shots, about one goal better than the chances he faced would suggest. Jacob Markstrom allowed 1.2 more goals than his 28 shots deserved.

The game turned in the third period. Justin Faulk scored on the power play at 2:08, and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård, the 2024 first-round pick, made it 4-2 forty-five seconds later. Sam Bennett pulled Florida within a goal at 16:40, but Emmitt Finnie sealed it into an empty net's worth of time, scoring with three seconds left. Faulk, picked 37th in 2010, took first star. Detroit leaves with a win built on a rookie's first goal and timely finishing, while Florida's three-game run is over despite out-shooting the Red Wings.
